You will work with our neighboring teams to ensure that our efforts aim to achieve a clearer architecture and boundaries between tech teams to support autonomy. Assume technical leadership within a tribe and own the most challenging tech decisions, including architecture, design, development, deployment, and operational excellence.
Support the teams in the architectural design and help to maintain architectural integrity in the scope of the tribe and beyond.

Solve software problems that have visible risks, roadblocks, and constraints. You will navigate an environment that is approximately 70% greenfield development and 30% legacy systems, managing dependencies, data quality, compliance, and architectural transformations.

Ideally, 10+ years of engineering experience, including 2+ years in a staff/principal level capacity and technical leadership.
Strong capability in working with different stakeholders and experience addressing physical world problems with software solutions.

A team player attitude and a passion for helping others grow through peer-to-peer mentoring, knowledge-sharing sessions, and advocating for best engineering practices, such as CI/CD, TDD, BDD, DDD, and Design Patterns.
An agile mindset with the ability to advocate for cross-functional collaboration.

Interacting with front-end developers, designers, product managers and our teams around the world is very much part of our day-to-day, so communication skills are vital. KNDS Deutschland Mission Electronics GmbH, a subsidiary of the KNDS Group, has been at the forefront of developing specialized IT solutions for over 40 years at its location in Konstanz. The company focuses on creating advanced, hardened IT systems tailored for the global security and defense sectors, as well as critical industrial environments. As a comprehensive provider, KNDS Deutschland Mission Electronics GmbH designs, develops, and implements complex hardware and software systems that facilitate secure information exchange and communication. Our commitment to innovation and quality has established us as a trusted partner for mission-critical applications worldwide. The company’s expertise spans the entire system lifecycle—from initial concept and requirements gathering to deployment, maintenance, and support—ensuring optimal performance and reliability in demanding operational contexts.

About The Role

We are seeking a dedicated Software Developer (m/w/d) with a focus on application development to join our dynamic team in Konstanz. In this role, you will be integral to the development of software solutions for military communication systems, rugged hardware platforms, and monitoring and testing systems. Your responsibilities will encompass designing, implementing, and documenting robust applications that meet stringent security and performance standards. You will work closely with cross-functional teams to analyze requirements, review system architectures, and ensure seamless integration and deployment of software solutions both in-house and on-site at customer locations. This position offers an excellent opportunity to contribute to innovative projects in a highly specialized field, working with cutting-edge technologies and multidisciplinary teams to deliver solutions that enhance security and operational effectiveness.

Qualifications

The ideal candidate will possess a degree in Computer Science, Technical Informatics, Communications Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related field. Proficiency in at least one programming language such as C++, C#, or Python is essential. Candidates should have a solid understanding of application development processes, including requirements analysis, system architecture review, and testing. Experience with collaboration platforms, version control systems, and integrated development environments is required. Additional expertise in user interface design, networked systems, Linux-based development, platform integration, or information security is advantageous. First professional experience in a relevant environment is preferred but not mandatory. Fluency in German, both written and spoken, is essential. The successful applicant will demonstrate a responsible, systematic approach to work, combined with creativity and strong teamwork skills.

Responsibilities

Design, develop, and document application software tailored for military communication, rugged hardware platforms, or monitoring and testing systems.
Conduct requirements analysis and participate in reviews of system architectures to ensure alignment with project goals and security standards.
Integrate, test, and commission software solutions both internally and at customer sites to ensure operational readiness and compliance.
Plan development tasks, including estimating timelines and resource requirements, to support project delivery deadlines.
Collaborate with multidisciplinary teams to ensure the seamless integration of software components within larger system architectures.
Maintain comprehensive documentation and provide ongoing support for deployed applications, including updates and troubleshooting.

Benefits

Secure employment with a reputable and stable employer in the defense and security industry.
Competitive salary aligned with the Bavarian IG Metall collective agreement.
Additional benefits including Christmas and holiday bonuses.
Opportunities for professional growth and career advancement within the company.
Generous vacation entitlement of 30 days per year.
Conveniently located office with excellent public transportation connections and available employee parking.
Company-sponsored retirement plan to support your long-term financial security.
On-site cafeteria providing meals and refreshments.
Flexible working hours with Gleitzeit arrangements to promote work-life balance.

Equal Opportunity

Description

The Role

Location:
Reigate / Hybrid

Reports to:
Mark Mamone

Peer relationships:
Head of Architecture, Platform & Engineering Enablement leadership, and Stack Engineering Leaders across ICT

WTW is seeking a technically credible engineering leader to mature and scale engineering capability across ICT. This is not a traditional Director of Engineering role: there are no direct reports. Instead, it is a strategic, deeply technical role focused on improving engineering consistency, software delivery maturity and effectiveness across five autonomous engineering stacks. They should be capable of being hands-on, for the purposes of reinforcing their strategic direction in the space of DevEx and being credible and authentic in the face of technical professionals.

The stacks have been given autonomy to improve delivery velocity. The next phase retains that autonomy while introducing the right level of shared practice, tooling consistency and technical governance. Success depends on technical depth and the ability to build consensus — influencing engineering decisions through credibility and evidence rather than formal authority, and being willing to roll up sleeves and get into technical and code-level problems when it helps move things forward.

Their scope is to ensure that, across 400+ technical professionals dispersed into teams aligned to Products, they are able to reinforce modern best practices — especially in an agentic world — and bring the teams along a journey to a more consistent, modern, AI-native software development lifecycle.

Key Responsibilities

Engineering practice & SDLC maturity: raise the quality and consistency of software design, development, testing and delivery; improve route-to-live, release management, quality gates and CI/CD; reduce manual effort where automation adds value.
Technical governance & consensus: provide constructive, hands-on challenge to engineering and architecture decisions; build alignment across stacks while respecting differing product, commercial and lifecycle needs; support pragmatic technical-debt strategies.
Tooling & developer experience: assess and improve developer experience; standardise and consolidate tooling where it creates clear value (including the move to GitHub as a strategic platform).
AI adoption across the SDLC: drive practical adoption of AI-enabled engineering across development, testing, review, documentation and support, aligned to governance and measurable outcomes.
Engineering metrics & insight: improve visibility of delivery health using frameworks such as DORA and the LinearB pilot; define WTW-specific “lighthouse metrics” that reflect real effectiveness, not activity.
Shared engineering capability: reduce duplication across stacks; promote reusable components, patterns and common engineering services where appropriate.

Technology Environment

The environment uses, or is moving towards: C#, .NET / .NET Core, Microsoft Azure, GitHub (an increasingly strategic platform), Azure DevOps, CI/CD pipelines and automation, and engineering analytics tooling including the LinearB pilot. The candidate should understand these well enough to challenge, guide and directly contribute to engineering direction.

What Success Looks Like

Greater consistency in engineering practices and stronger technical alignment across stacks.
Improved SDLC maturity, better CI/CD and reduced manual effort, through the adoption of AI, automation and other mechanisms
Better developer experience and pragmatic tooling standardisation where it adds value.
Clearer engineering metrics and improved visibility of delivery health.
Increased reuse of engineering capability and greater adoption of AI-enabled practices.
A healthy balance between stack autonomy and organisational consistency.

This role suits a technical CTO-style leader who succeeds through credibility, judgement and consensus rather than line authority — and who stays close enough to the methodologies associated with software engineering and where necessary, the code, to challenge, guide and, when needed, get directly involved in solving technical problems.

Strong technical depth: able to hold their own with Stack Engineering Leaders and dive into architecture, code and delivery detail when it adds value.
A natural consensus-builder: challenges decisions constructively, aligns strong personalities, and creates momentum without unnecessary friction.
An excellent communicator who can simplify complex engineering topics for any audience.
Outcome-focused, pragmatic and comfortable balancing consistency with stack autonomy.

Essential technical experience across several of modern software engineering practices; enterprise-scale delivery and SDLC optimisation; CI/CD and deployment automation; cloud-native engineering; application architecture and technical design; secure, quality-led delivery; engineering metrics; technical-debt management; and AI adoption within engineering.

Background & Industry

There is no rigid career blueprint; breadth is an advantage. Purpose of the Role

Out client operates high volume debt recovery services supported by a technology platform built on Microsoft Azure, with SQL Server at its core and a range of API and file-based integrations connecting the Group to its clients and suppliers.

The Software Developer will work alongside the Group Technology Director, with primary responsibility for designing, building and publishing APIs, supported by ownership of the Azure infrastructure and SQL environment those APIs run on. The role suits a developer who is comfortable working independently: given an objective, you will plan your own approach, flag anything that needs sign-off, and deliver against it, with your work reviewed on completion rather than at every step. We want your view on the approach itself, not just delivery against it — if you see a better way, we want to hear it before you build, not after.

Principal Responsibilities

> Design, build and publish APIs supporting the exchange of data between the Group's systems, clients and suppliers, from initial design through to live release.

> Take ownership of the full lifecycle of each API: versioning, documentation, testing and ongoing maintenance.

> Manage and maintain the Group's Azure infrastructure supporting these APIs, including application services, databases, networking and monitoring.

> Develop and optimise SQL, including queries, stored procedures, data corrections and reporting extracts against production-scale datasets.

> Plan your own work: translate objectives into a short written approach, raise risks or dependencies early, and proceed with minimal supervision once the approach is agreed.

> Build and maintain deployment pipelines for the APIs and services you own.

> Provide technical enablement to the wider business, including supporting the Operations department's AI and process improvement function with API access and data provision.

> Monitor, investigate and resolve incidents and issues across the systems you are responsible for.

> Produce and maintain clear technical documentation for all APIs, infrastructure and solutions delivered.

> Operate at all times within the security, data protection and compliance standards expected of a regulated debt recovery business.

Person Specification

Essential

> Solid, demonstrable experience designing, building and publishing APIs in a mainstream language [e.g. C#/.NET, Python or Node.js], through professional work or substantial personal projects — ideally projects where you decided the approach yourself, not just built to someone else’s spec.

Business analysis: understanding how a financial institution works, mapping its processes, and turning a vague request into a clear specification
ML engineering: building, evaluating and improving models, from classic prediction models to fine-tuned LLMs
Software engineering: building the APIs, integrations and applications that put models into real workflows, then deploying and maintaining them

Nobody arrives strong in all three. We hire people who are solid in at least one and eager to grow into the others.

Sit with client stakeholders to understand a workflow and identify where AI creates measurable value
Build prediction models and ML-based document analysis
Fine-tune LLMs to power conversational interfaces over the client's data

Design the APIs and integrations that connect your models to the client's systems
Deploy, monitor and improve what you've built once it's live

Communicating technical work clearly to non-technical stakeholders

new_jobs.description:
Multivative ist ein österreichisches Startup und das Technologieunternehmen hinter Pick2Place. Wir fertigen Elektronik-Prototypen für Entwicklungsteams in ganz Europa und zeigen, dass schnelles, flexibles und kostengünstiges Prototyping auch hier möglich ist. Der Schlüssel dazu ist Automatisierung: Ein Prototyp wird online mit wenigen Klicks bestellt, unsere Software und selbstentwickelten Maschinen übernehmen den Großteil der Arbeit, und ein paar Tage später liegt die fertige Platine beim Kunden. Wir sind ein kleines technisches Team in Vorarlberg und Graz und bauen fast alles selbst, von der Weboberfläche bis zur Bestückungsmaschine. Wir stehen noch am Anfang, wachsen aber schnell, und unser Ziel ist klar: der führende Elektronik-Prototypenfertiger in Europa zu werden.

Aufgaben

Du entwickelst die Software unserer Bestückungs- und Inspektionsmaschinen weiter: Bewegungssteuerung, Bildverarbeitung, Kalibrierung (C#, .NET).
Du baust und verbesserst unsere Machine-Vision-Pipeline, von der Kameraansteuerung und Beleuchtung bis zur Bauteilerkennung und optischen Inspektion.
Du bringst ML-Modelle vom Prototyp in den Produktionsbetrieb und sorgst dafür, dass sie an der Maschine zuverlässig laufen.
Du triffst Architekturentscheidungen selbstständig und übernimmst Verantwortung für die technische Umsetzung.
Du setzt AI-Tools im Alltag ein, um schneller und besser zu entwickeln.
Du stehst regelmäßig an der Maschine, testest direkt an der Hardware und arbeitest eng mit unserem Mechanik- und Elektronikteam zusammen.

Qualifikationen

Erfahrung mit C# und .NET, idealerweise in der Ansteuerung von Hardware oder in Echtzeit-nahen Anwendungen.
Grundlagen in Bildverarbeitung oder Machine Vision (OpenCV, Kamerasysteme, Beleuchtung). Erfahrung mit ML-basierter Erkennung ist ein Plus, kein Muss.
Ein gutes Gefühl für Architektur. Du kannst begründen, warum du dich für eine Lösung entscheidest.
Freude daran, mit echter Hardware zu arbeiten. Wenn etwas nicht funktioniert, gehst du zur Maschine und schaust nach.
Du nutzt LLMs und Coding-Agents selbstverständlich in deiner Arbeit und hast Lust, das weiter auszureizen.
Du willst in einem wachsenden Startup mitwachsen, Verantwortung übernehmen und Dinge selbst in die Hand nehmen.
Deutsch oder Englisch, beides ist bei uns im Alltag.

Du musst nicht alle Punkte abhaken. Ein motivierter Engineer, der schnell lernt und wirklich etwas bauen will, ist uns wichtiger als ein perfekter Lebenslauf.
